venues.name: Beau-Rivage Genève
venues.note: The city's grande dame since 1865, fifth-generation family-owned, lake-facing, and quite simply the Geneva address.

venues.name: Four Seasons Hotel des Bergues Genève
venues.area: Rive Droite / Les Bergues (Quai des Bergues)
venues.note: Geneva's oldest grand hotel, open since 1834, a neoclassical house on the Rhône with Four Seasons polish.

venues.name: Mandarin Oriental, Geneva
venues.area: Rive Droite / on the Rhône (Quai Turrettini)
venues.note: Mandarin Oriental precision on the riverbank, one of only two Forbes Five-Star houses in the city.

venues.name: The Ritz-Carlton Hotel de la Paix, Geneva
venues.note: An 1865 lakefront landmark reborn under The Ritz-Carlton, grand, contemporary and squarely on the water.

venues.name: La Réserve Genève Hotel & Spa
venues.area: Bellevue / lakefront, just north of the city
venues.note: A Jacques Garcia-designed lakeside resort in its own park, a colonial-safari fantasy a short drive from the centre.

venues.name: Hôtel d'Angleterre
venues.note: An intimate Red Carnation townhouse on the lake, English warmth and a famous piano bar, at a gentler scale than the palaces.

venues.name: Hôtel Métropole Genève
venues.note: A family-owned Belle Époque house on the left-bank lakefront, dignified, discreet and quietly grand.
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World

venues.name: Hôtel Les Armures
venues.note: A 17th-century house at the very heart of the medieval Old Town, history, stone and quiet a step from the cathedral.

venues.name: InterContinental Genève
venues.area: Grand-Saconnex / near the UN and airport
venues.note: The city's diplomatic-summit hotel, large, capable and close to the Palais des Nations and the airport.

venues.name: L'Atelier Robuchon
venues.note: Geneva's only two-star table, the late Joël Robuchon's counter concept, exact and theatrical, around an open kitchen.

venues.name: Domaine de Châteauvieux
venues.note: Philippe Chevrier's country auberge among the vineyards, a Geneva institution, and GaultMillau's highest-scored table in the region.

venues.name: Il Lago
venues.area: Four Seasons Hotel des Bergues, Rive Droite / Les Bergues
venues.note: Refined northern-Italian cooking in the Four Seasons' gilded room, classical, generous and beautifully served.

venues.name: Fiskebar
venues.area: The Ritz-Carlton Hotel de la Paix, Rive Droite / lakefront
venues.note: A Nordic seafood enclave inside the Ritz-Carlton, clean, precise, sea-led cooking with a Scandinavian hand.

venues.name: Tsé Fung
venues.note: Switzerland's only Michelin-starred Chinese restaurant, Cantonese refinement in Jacques Garcia's lakeside resort.

venues.name: Le Cigalon
venues.note: The Bessire family's seafood room, first-class fish flown from Roscoff and Audierne, cooked with flawless craft for nearly thirty years.

venues.name: La Chaumière
venues.note: Serge Labrosse's creative, modern cooking in a converted farmhouse, refined food in an easy country setting.

venues.name: L'Aparté
venues.note: Armel Bedouet's tiny fifteen-seat room, intimate, precise, produce-led fine dining for a handful of guests.

venues.name: La Micheline
venues.note: Andres Arocena's bright, seasonal bistronomy, a young star at the new Eaux-Vives station quarter.

venues.name: Tosca
venues.note: Ivan Baretti's precise Tuscan cooking, Arpège-trained technique in an intimate Eaux-Vives room.

venues.name: Windows
venues.note: Well-crafted French cooking with the Jet d'Eau and Mont Blanc framed in the window, a lovely lakefront room.

venues.name: Osteria della Bottega
venues.note: Seasonal Italian with handmade pasta at its heart, an open kitchen and chic industrial room in the Old Town.

venues.name: Le Dorian
venues.note: A well-priced newcomer with real flavour and craft, the kind of honest, refined cooking the Bib rewards.

venues.name: Natürlich
venues.note: Sustainable, produce-led cooking on the river, fresh, local ingredients handled with a light, honest touch.

venues.name: The Jet d'Eau
venues.note: Geneva's signature: a 140-metre plume of lake water shooting up from the harbour, visible from across the city and lit at night. Ask your driver to time an evening lakeside walk along the Quai Gustave-Ador so the children see it catch the last light.

venues.name: CGN Belle Époque paddle-steamer cruise
venues.note: Board one of the fleet of restored 1900s-era steamers at the Jardin Anglais or Mont-Blanc landing and glide past vineyards, châteaux and the Alps with a private table for lunch. The unhurried pace and top-deck views suit a multi-generational family, and the galley will manage vegetarian requests with notice.

venues.name: Bains des Pâquis
venues.note: The beloved public bathing pier reaching into the lake beside the Jet d'Eau, with wooden decks, a sauna and hammam in winter, and a famously good fondue in the little buvette. Unpretentious and thoroughly local, it is where Geneva actually relaxes.

venues.name: Jardin Anglais & the Flower Clock
venues.note: The lakeside promenade where Geneva's most photographed emblem, the Horloge Fleurie, is planted in thousands of live blooms that change with the season, its second hand the longest in the world. A gentle, pram-friendly stroll right by the Jet d'Eau.

venues.name: Île Rousseau
venues.note: A leafy islet in the middle of the Rhône, reached by a short footbridge, with the seated statue of philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau under old trees and swans on the water. A quiet green pause in the very heart of the city.

venues.name: St Pierre Cathedral & its towers
venues.note: The Old Town's Reformation-era cathedral where John Calvin preached, its climbable towers rewarding the effort with the finest rooftop panorama of the lake, the Alps and the tiled roofs below. Beneath it, the archaeological site reveals Roman and early-Christian layers.

venues.name: Place du Bourg-de-Four
venues.note: Geneva's oldest square, a sloping cobbled space of cafés, a central fountain and antique shops that has been a marketplace since Roman times. The natural spot to sit with a coffee and watch Old Town life unfold.

venues.name: Maison Tavel
venues.note: The oldest private house in Geneva, a 12th-century stone mansion now a museum of the city's history, whose highlight is the vast Magnin relief model of 1850s Geneva before its ramparts fell. A calm, uncrowded window into how the city grew.

venues.name: The Reformation Wall
venues.note: A 100-metre monument set into the old ramparts of Parc des Bastions, its five-metre statues of Calvin, Farel, Bèze and Knox marking Geneva's role as the 'Protestant Rome'. The surrounding park has giant chess boards the children can play on.

venues.name: Parc des Bastions
venues.note: The elegant park at the foot of the Old Town, home to the Reformation Wall, the University of Geneva's founding buildings and rows of giant open-air chess sets. Shaded, central and made for an easy afternoon.

venues.name: Patek Philippe Museum
venues.note: A private, hushed temple to watchmaking assembled by the Stern family, spanning five centuries of timepieces, enamels and automata across four floors, with Patek's own masterpieces on the top. Essential for the collector and a discreet, world-class hour for anyone with an interest in horology.

venues.name: Rue du Rhône watch and jewellery boutiques
venues.note: Geneva's golden mile: the flagship maisons of Patek Philippe, Rolex, Vacheron Constantin, Cartier and their peers line the Rue du Rhône and adjacent lanes. Private appointments and after-hours viewings are the norm for serious clients, arranged discreetly.

venues.name: Cité du Temps
venues.note: A free exhibition space on a bridge over the Rhône dedicated to time and Swiss watchmaking, with the Planet Swatch collection and rotating horological shows. A light, engaging counterpoint to the grand watch museums, right in the centre.

venues.name: International Red Cross & Red Crescent Museum
venues.note: A moving, superbly designed museum opposite the UN telling the story of humanitarian action through three chambers on defending dignity, restoring family links and reducing natural risks. Sober and powerful, and a reminder of why Geneva matters to the world.

venues.name: Palais des Nations (UN Geneva)
venues.note: The European headquarters of the United Nations, its grand halls and the ceiling of the Human Rights room open to guided visits set within a park roamed by peacocks. Bring passports; a private guide smooths the security and brings the diplomacy alive.

venues.name: The Broken Chair
venues.note: A 12-metre wooden chair with a shattered leg standing before the UN, a stark monument against landmines and cluster bombs. It stops every visitor for a moment and photographs beautifully against the flags.

venues.name: CERN Science Gateway
venues.note: The Renzo Piano-designed visitor centre of the world's great particle-physics laboratory, with free interactive exhibitions on the universe, the quantum world and the Large Hadron Collider. Genuinely thrilling for curious teenagers and science-minded travellers; registration is free but required.

venues.name: Musée d'art et d'histoire (MAH)
venues.note: One of Switzerland's largest museums, an encyclopaedic collection of fine art, antiquities and armour from Hodler and Corot to Egyptian and Roman treasures. Vast and serene, with an inflatable art installation currently animating its courtyard.

venues.name: Conservatoire et Jardin botaniques (Botanical Garden)
venues.note: Twenty-eight free hectares of themed gardens, greenhouses, an arboretum and a small animal park on the lake's edge, kept to a high standard. An easy, restful outing that works for grandparents and small children alike.

venues.name: Carouge
venues.note: Geneva's 'little Italy', a Sardinian-built quarter of low pastel houses, leafy inner courtyards, artisan workshops and independent cafés often called the city's Greenwich Village. The place to browse jewellers and design studios far from the tourist run, then linger over lunch on a shaded square.

venues.name: Parc La Grange & its rose garden
venues.note: The city's most beautiful park, an 18th-century estate above the lake whose historic Roseraie holds thousands of rose bushes in hundreds of varieties, at their peak in June. Free summer concerts play in the grounds.

venues.name: Parc des Eaux-Vives
venues.note: An elegant lakeside park adjoining La Grange, with sweeping lawns, old trees and long views to the Jet d'Eau and Mont Blanc. Its 18th-century villa houses a fine restaurant, making it a natural pairing with a garden walk.

venues.name: Mont Salève cable car
venues.note: A five-minute cable-car ride up 'Geneva's balcony' on the French side to 1,100 metres, with the whole city, the lake and, on clear days, Mont Blanc laid out below. Passports needed; the summit has walking trails and a viewpoint restaurant.

venues.name: Plainpalais flea market
venues.note: One of Europe's largest flea markets, sprawling across the great open plaza every Wednesday and Saturday, from watch parts and vintage Swiss enamel to furniture and curiosities. A treasure hunt for the collector's eye, best in the morning.

venues.name: Villa Diodati (exterior)
venues.note: The lakeside mansion above Geneva where Mary Shelley conceived Frankenstein during the stormy summer of 1816 with Byron. Privately owned so only the exterior and surrounding paths can be seen, but the literary aura and Cologny's grand villas make it a rewarding detour by car.

venues.name: Auer chocolatier
venues.note: A family chocolate house since 1939, tucked in the shopping streets and famed for its amandes princesses and delicate pralines. A small, authentic institution for a discreet gift or a private tasting.

venues.name: Favarger chocolate
venues.note: Geneva's historic chocolate maker, run by the same family since 1826, whose Avelines and Nougalines are local legends; its lakeside Carouge factory can be visited. An easy, crowd-pleasing stop for the family that travels with a sweet tooth.

venues.name: Le Chat-Botté
venues.note: The Michelin-starred dining room of the grand Beau-Rivage hotel, refined French cuisine with a lake terrace and a dedicated vegetarian tasting menu. The natural choice for a formal family dinner where the setting matters as much as the plate.

venues.name: Old Town antiquarian and gallery lanes
venues.note: The steep cobbled streets around Grand-Rue and Rue des Granges hide antiquarian booksellers, art galleries and Rousseau's birthplace at No. 40. A slow, elegant amble through the city's most historic quarter.

venues.name: Quai du Mont-Blanc grand-hotel promenade
venues.note: The stately waterfront where Geneva's palace hotels line up facing the Jet d'Eau and the Brunswick Monument, with the flower-lined Bains-Anglais steps and lake views. A classic evening stroll from the Beau-Rivage and the Four Seasons doorsteps.

venues.name: Lausanne & the Olympic Museum
venues.note: The Olympic capital across the lake, its lakeside Olympic Museum set in sculpture gardens tracing the Games from antiquity to now, a hit with children. Pair it with Ouchy's waterfront and the medieval cathedral in the upper town.

venues.name: Annecy
venues.note: The 'Venice of the Alps' across the border, a jewel of flower-draped canals, a lakeside old town and turquoise water framed by peaks. A relaxed, walkable day of markets, gelato and boat rides; passports required for the border.

venues.name: Chamonix & Aiguille du Midi
venues.note: The legendary alpine town at the foot of Mont Blanc, from where the Aiguille du Midi cable car climbs to 3,842 metres and a glass 'Step into the Void' box over the glaciers. Unforgettable high-mountain drama within a day of Geneva; a private driver makes the border and timings effortless.

venues.name: Gruyères
venues.note: A perfectly preserved medieval hilltop village with a hilltop castle, famous for its AOP cheese dairy and the nearby Cailler chocolate factory at Broc. Cheese, chocolate and a fairy-tale walled town in one outing that delights children and adults.

venues.name: Salève and lakeside private helicopter flight
venues.note: A scenic helicopter transfer or flightseeing loop over the lake, the vineyards and the Mont Blanc massif, arranged from Geneva airport. The most spectacular way to grasp the geography, and a memorable treat for a family celebration.

venues.name: MEG, Musée d'ethnographie de Genève
venues.note: An award-winning ethnography museum in striking modern architecture, showing world cultures through a collection of over 70,000 objects. Thoughtful, uncrowded and a strong wet-weather alternative to the lake.
credentials: European Museum of the Year Award winner (2017)

venues.name: Fondation Baur, Museum of Far Eastern Art
venues.note: A discreet town-mansion museum of Chinese and Japanese art, jades, ceramics and Samurai swords, one of Europe's finest such collections. A serene, little-known gem for a quiet cultured hour.

venues.name: Barbier-Mueller Museum
venues.note: A small, exquisite private museum of tribal and ancient art from Africa, Oceania and the Americas, superbly lit and curated in the heart of the Old Town. For the connoisseur, one of the world's great collections of its kind.

venues.name: Bodmer Foundation library & museum
venues.note: A jaw-dropping private library above the lake at Cologny holding a Gutenberg Bible, Shakespeare folios and papyrus fragments among world literature's treasures. A cultural pilgrimage for bibliophiles, in one of Geneva's grandest residential enclaves.
credentials: UNESCO Memory of the World collection

venues.name: Leopard Bar, Hôtel d'Angleterre
venues.note: A clubby, low-lit lakefront piano bar, live jazz most nights and one of the city's most characterful drinks.
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN One-Key, Forbes 4-Star hotel, a Geneva institution

venues.name: Le Bar des Bergues, Four Seasons
venues.note: The Four Seasons' elegant bar, a considered cocktail in one of the city's most polished rooms.
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN Two-Key, Forbes 5-Star hotel

venues.name: Le Bar, The Woodward
venues.note: An intimate, jewel-box bar inside the city's most exclusive hotel, discreet, dressed-up and beautifully made.
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN Three-Key hotel (Auberge Resorts Collection)
